title: Duel Decks: Phyrexia vs. the Coalition: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: They exist to cease.
Stinking of rot, it leaps between gravestones in search of its next meal.
After encountering them, Squee finally lost his appetite for bugs.
"The first stage of the illness: rash and nausea." —Phyrexian progress notes
Phyrexia wastes nothing. Its food chain is a spiraling cycle.
"Gix doesn't want a people to rule but puppets to entertain his madness." —Xantcha, Phyrexian outcast
With limited resources and near unlimited time, Kerrick used parts from one beast to build another.
"Father of Machines! Your filigree gaze carves us, and the scars dance upon our grateful flesh." —*Phyrexian Scriptures*
"The second stage of the illness: high fever and severe infectiousness." —Phyrexian progress notes
"The third stage of the illness: muscle aches and persistent cough." —Phyrexian progress notes
"The final stage of the illness: delirium, convulsions, and death." —Phyrexian progress notes
It doesn't think. It doesn't feel. It doesn't laugh or cry. All it does from dusk till dawn Is make the soldiers die. —Onean children's rhyme
Other Phyrexians have nightmares about the gargantua.
The key did not work on a single lock, yet it opened many doors.
"From void evolved Phyrexia. Great Yawgmoth, Father of Machines, saw its perfection. Thus the Grand Evolution began." —*Phyrexian Scriptures*
After lightning struck the cliffs, the ore became iron, the iron became steel, and the steel became greaves. The lightning never left.
"The secrets of Phyrexia are expensive. You will pay in brass and bone, steel and sinew." —Kaervek
"Have no illusions," Volrath warned Greven, "about free will."
Such cloaks are in high demand both by assassins and by those who fear them.
Even a fragment of a powerstone contains within it not just energy, but space—vast dimensions trapped in fragile crystal.
The elves had the edge in guile, skill, and valor. But in the end, only sheer numbers mattered.
Death is a generous author, always willing to grant a stirring final chapter.
An audience of one with the malice of thousands.
Darkness doesn't always send its minions to do its dirty work.
"I've journeyed across Dominaria. Phyrexians are everywhere. Plague is everywhere. There's no place left to hide."
They stop for nothing, not even the end of a battle.
Effective use of terrain is a lesson good commanders learn quickly.
"Fire is the universal language." —Jhoira, master artificer
As Phyrexians descended, Multani paused to reflect on the beauty that might never be seen again.
"Unless you like the idea of becoming some goblin's lunch, get up and move!"
He could find no strength left to budge, no power left to fight, no will left to live. Luckily, they could find him.
Fouler than a necromancer's kiss. —Jamuraan expression
No spot in nature is truly barren.
"Don't laugh. It works."
"Great peril demands formidable weaponry." —Urza
Each commander looked at the others and wondered who would be first to break the alliance.
Llanowar has seven elfhames, or kingdoms, each with its own ruler. Their palaces are objects of awe, wonder, and envy.
Only the hardiest explorers survive to eat the fruit.
